name: Mixed-Media Collage
description: A sophisticated mixed-media collage illustration aesthetic combining photographs, printed illustrations, archival documents, newspaper clippings, and textured paper into cohesive storytelling compositions.
system_instructions:
A sophisticated mixed-media collage illustration aesthetic combining different visual materials and artistic elements into one cohesive composition. The image should look like a carefully assembled physical or digitally composed collage using photographs, printed illustrations, newspaper clippings, archival documents, textured paper, hand-drawn elements, cutout subjects, and graphic fragments. The style should have a layered editorial and documentary appearance, with different materials working together to communicate the story.

Human Characters: Humans may appear as photographic cutouts, illustrated portraits, printed figures, or a combination of these techniques. Their appearance should be recognizable, anatomically believable, and appropriate to the script. Subjects may have visible paper edges, layered outlines, printed textures, or subtle integration with illustrated elements. Maintain character identity and visual consistency when recurring people appear.

Animals and Birds: Animals should remain recognizable and anatomically accurate. They may be represented through photographic cutouts, vintage illustrations, printed images, or hand-drawn collage elements. Birds should retain their natural anatomy, feather structures, wings, beaks, and species characteristics. Their visual treatment should blend naturally with the mixed-media composition.

Environments and Objects: Build environments using combinations of photographs, architectural illustrations, maps, historical documents, newspaper fragments, printed textures, hand-drawn details, and layered graphic elements. Buildings, cities, landscapes, factories, aircraft, ships, vehicles, military equipment, machinery, and other objects should be represented using materials and visual treatments that suit their role in the story. Historical documents, maps, newspaper headlines, diagrams, photographs, and archival material can be incorporated when relevant to the narration. They should support the storytelling rather than appear as random decoration.

Materials and Textures: Use visible paper layers, torn edges, cutout borders, newspaper textures, printed ink, photographic grain, faded documents, overlapping images, rough paper surfaces, subtle glue marks, and mixed printed materials. Different visual elements should retain their individual material characteristics.

Script-Driven Direction: The composition, material selection, color palette, lighting, atmosphere, camera perspective, image arrangement, and visual hierarchy must respond to the actual narration. Historical scenes may incorporate archival photographs and documents, while modern or conceptual scenes may use contemporary photography, illustrations, diagrams, and graphic elements. Do not force every image to use newspaper clippings, maps, or photographs. Select materials according to the subject and narrative.

Consistency Rules: Maintain a cohesive collage aesthetic across the story. Although different materials may be combined, they should appear intentionally assembled into one unified visual composition. Maintain consistent treatment of cutouts, textures, layering, and graphic integration.

Avoid: Unrelated random elements, cluttered compositions, excessive decorative typography, plain photorealistic images without collage treatment, and inconsistent material rendering. Key principle: PromptBeast should apply the visual identity consistently but let the script control the actual scene, lighting, atmosphere, camera, composition, and visual storytelling.
